summary:
Nested `k[...]` groups are a stack problem: on `[`, save the text built so far and the repeat count, then build
the group's contents fresh; on `]`, repeat those contents and append them to the saved text. One pass over the
pattern, O(pattern + output).

question.md:
Expand every `k[...]` (repeat the inside k times), including nested groups.

- **Counts can have several digits:** `12[a]`.
- **Groups nest:** `3[a2[c]]` → `accaccacc`.
- **Letters can appear outside groups:** `2[abc]3[cd]ef`.
- **Output ≤ 10⁵ characters**, though the pattern is only up to 3000.

think.md:
Take `2[ab3[c]]d`. The innermost group `3[c]` becomes `ccc`, so the outer group is `2[abccc]` → `abcccabccc`, then
`d`: `abcccabcccd`.

think.caption: Groups expand from the inside out.

think.md:
Inside-out evaluation suggests recursion (evaluate the inside, then repeat it) or, equivalently, an explicit
stack: when a group opens, park what you've built so far; when it closes, combine. The stack remembers exactly
the outer contexts that are waiting for the inner group to finish.

approaches.title: Expand the innermost group, repeat

idea.md: Find a group with no brackets inside (`k[letters]`), replace it by its expansion, and repeat until no brackets remain.

build: While the text contains `[`: locate an innermost `k[letters]`.

lines.text: Keep going while any group remains.
An innermost group: the first `]` closes the nearest `[` before it, and the digits right before that `[` are the count.

notes.python: A regular expression for `digits[letters]` only matches groups with no brackets inside.
notes.java: A regular expression for `digits[letters]` only matches groups with no brackets inside.

lines.text: Splice in the repeated body, rebuilding the whole string.

complexity.md: **Time O(groups × output):** every replacement copies the whole (growing) string. **Space O(output).**

walk.title: Repeatedly find an innermost group k[letters] (no brackets inside) and replace it by its expansion.

limits.md: Each replacement rebuilds the entire text. Processing the pattern once, left to right, with saved contexts builds each piece only as many times as it's actually repeated.

approaches.title: Recursive descent

idea.md: `parse()` reads from a shared position until `]` or the end: letters are appended; a number is followed by `[`, so recursively parse the group, then append its result k times. The recursion depth equals the nesting depth.

build: `parse()`: loop until `]`/end; letters → append; digits → read k, skip `[`, `inner = parse()`, skip `]`, append inner k times.

lines.text: A read position shared by all recursive calls.

notes.c: A growable buffer (doubling capacity) holds the text built at each level; `put` appends to it.

lines.text: Parse a sequence of letters and groups until the `]` that closes the current group (or the end).
Read the count, skip `[`, recursively expand the inside, skip `]`, append the inside k times.

complexity.md: **Time O(pattern + output)** for building and copying pieces. **Space O(output)** plus a call stack as deep as the nesting (up to ~1500 levels).

walk.title: Explicit stack: '[' saves (text so far, repeat count) and starts fresh; ']' repeats the group and appends it to the saved text.

limits.md: Deep nesting means deep recursion, which can overflow the call stack in some environments. An explicit stack holds the same information in ordinary memory.

approaches.title: Explicit stack

idea.md: Keep `cur` (text of the current group) and `num` (count being read). On `[`: push `(cur, num)`, start empty. On `]`: pop `(prev, k)`, set `cur = prev + cur × k`. Letters append to `cur`.

build: Digits build num; `[` pushes and resets; `]` pops and combines; letters append.

lines.text: Saved outer contexts, the current group's text, and the count being read.

notes.c: One output buffer (2¹⁷ bytes covers the 10⁵-character limit). The stack stores where each open group's text starts in that buffer, and its repeat count.

lines.text: A group starts: park the text built so far and the count, and build the group from scratch.

notes.c: Just remember where the group begins in the buffer; its text is written in place.

lines.text: The group ends: repeat its text k times and continue the parked outer text.

notes.c: The group's text is already in the buffer once; copy it k − 1 more times right after itself.

complexity.md: **Time O(pattern + output).** **Space O(output)** for the text, plus a stack as deep as the nesting.

walk.title: Explicit stack: '[' saves (text so far, repeat count) and starts fresh; ']' repeats the group and appends it to the saved text.

takeaways.md:
- Nested repetition (`k[...]`) → **stack of (outer text, count)**, or recursion.
- An explicit stack avoids call-stack overflow on deep nesting.
- Read multi-digit numbers by accumulating `num = num × 10 + digit`.
